CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI V.HOSMANI  ORAL JUDGMENT Challenging judgment and award dated 22.12.2014 passed by Senior Civil Judge, Saundatti at Saundatti ('Tribunal' for short) in MVC no.2039/2012, this appeal is filed.
2.
Sri GN Raichur, learned counsel for appellant submitted that, appeal was by insurer challenging finding of Tribunal on liability.

It was submitted, as per claimant, on 27.10.2011 at 06.45 p.m., when claimant was riding motorcycle no.KA-24/J-2390 on Ugaragol-Yallammanagudda road, a rider of another motorcycle no.KA-24/K-9244 rode it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against claimant's motorcycle causing accident.
In accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries.

Despite treatment at Government Hospital, Saundatti and thereafter at Dr.Sitaram Mokhashi Memorial Hospital, Saptapur, Dharwad, he did not recover fully and sustained 'loss of earning capacity' and lost amenities.

Therefore he filed claim NC: 2026:KHC-D:4930 HC-KAR petition under Section 166 National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Ganeshgouda on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46336973/
2 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act' for short) against owner and insurer of offending motorcycle.

sentences.text: 3. On service of notice, claim petition was opposed on all counts.
Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and record of evidence.
Claimant examined himself as PW1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P16.

Insurer examined its official as RW1 and got marked Exs.R1 to R4.
4.

On consideration, Tribunal held accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of insured motorcycle and claimant was entitled for compensation of Rs.70,300/- with interest at 6% per annum from insurer.
Aggrieved, present appeal was filed.
5. Sole ground urged by insurer in appeal is that, at time of accident, rider of insured motorcycle did not have valid and effective driving licence and therefore insurer could not be held liable.

It was elaborated by stating that a specific contention was taken in objections and insurer had issued notice as per Ex.R1 to insured for production of documents including driving licence of rider at time of accident.
It was submitted said notice was served as per Ex.R2.
Despite same, insured failed to NC: 2026:KHC-D:4930 HC-KAR produce driving licence thereby substantiating insurer's contention.
While passing impugned award, Tribunal overlooked said aspect and fastened liability.

Therefore, interference was warranted.
6.
There is no representation for respondents.

7. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment, award and record.
8.

From above, only point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether tribunal was justified in holding insurer liable to pay compensation?"

Same is answered partly in affirmative for following:
REASONS 9.
At outset, there is no dispute about occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle leading to claimant sustaining grievous injuries and being entitled for compensation.
There is no challenge of award on quantum.

Perusal of written statement filed by insurer reveals that a specific contention about rider of NC: 2026:KHC-D:4930 HC-KAR insured vehicle not possessing valid and effective driving license as on date of accident is specifically taken.
Insurer has also examined its official as RW1 and got marked copy of notice issued to insured along with acknowledgment of service of notice on insured for production of driving licence.

10. Though Ex.P6-charge sheet does not reveal rider being prosecuted for causing accident without driving licence, records reveal that claimant had produced photocopy of driving licence but failed to produce certified extract.
Under above circumstances, adverse inference requires to be drawn.

However, since claimant is a third party to contract of insurance, in view of ratio laid down on by Full Bench of this Court in case of New India Assurance Company Limited v. Yallavva & Anr.1,
National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Ganeshgouda on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46336973/
3 insurer would require to answer claim of third party and thereafter recover compensation from insured.

sentences.text:
In view of above following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
2020 (2) KCCR 1405 (FB) NC: 2026:KHC-D:4930 HC-KAR ii. Judgment and award dated 22.12.2014 passed by Senior Civil Judge, Saundatti, in MVC no.2039/2012, is modified.

iii . Insurer is held liable to pay compensation to claimant as assessed in first instance and thereafter would be at liberty to recover same from insured without need for separate proceedings.
iv. Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to Tribunal for payment.
v. Balance amount to be deposited within six weeks.
vi. On deposit, compensation amount is ordered to be released in favour of claimant.

Sd/-
(RAVI V.HOSMANI) JUDGE EM, CT:VP
